chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Muhrim (one in Ihram) who hunts game, he said: 'Upon him is the expiation for whatever he catches.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: One in the state of Ihram, a ritual status for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and expiation for a person in Ihram who hunts an animal?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that the obligation of expiation applies individually to each distinct game animal caught, rather than as a single lump sum, a point of discussion among Shia jurists regarding the definition of 'each' in this context. It underscores the sanctity of the sacred boundaries (Haram) during pilgrimage, linking the physical act of hunting to spiritual accountability. The ruling serves as a practical guideline for pilgrims to maintain ritual purity and mindfulness of divine restrictions during the sacred months.
